hero.headline: Medicare fraud scheme linked to Delray Beach targets same seniors twice through new Texas company
hero.body:
A Russian national connected to a Delray Beach medical equipment company accused of Medicare fraud allegedly continued submitting bills to the federal health program through a new Texas business after the original company's payments were suspended. Mike and Connie Parrett were among dozens of Medicare recipients who contacted WPTV after Sunshine Senior Solutions submitted fraudulent claims in Connie's name for medical equipment she never requested or received. More than a year later, the Parretts received another Medicare statement, this time billing Mike for services through a company called Centurion Superior Medical in Austin, Texas.

Federal investigators have connected Centurion to the same individuals behind Sunshine Senior Solutions. A criminal complaint names Nika Machutadze, a Russian national, as someone who allegedly used Centurion to bill Medicare in 2025 after the government suspended payments to Sunshine Senior Solutions in late 2024. Business records show Machutadze listed as an owner of both companies. Mike Parrett's Medicare statement revealed that two of six charges from Centurion were denied, though all charges appeared during 2025. The bills primarily involved catheters spread across multiple invoices, mirroring the original fraudulent charges his wife had received.

Dr. David Maimon, a cyberfraud expert who has studied the Sunshine Senior Solutions case, explains that criminals typically maintain lists of victim identities and frequently share these lists with other fraudsters, making seniors vulnerable to repeated targeting. Maimon advises potential victims to freeze their credit and consider purchasing identity protection services. He highlighted the Justice Department's newly created National Fraud Enforcement Division, which focuses specifically on Medicare fraud investigations, as evidence that the government is treating these crimes with greater urgency.

Machutadze was charged with conspiracy to commit money laundering in January 2026 and arrested in Texas the following month. He remains in custody as his case proceeds through federal court in West Palm Beach. The case illustrates how medical equipment fraud schemes can operate across multiple states and target the same victims repeatedly, even after initial fraudulent activity has been detected and suspended by federal authorities.

cards.headline: Tire shop technician killed after vehicle falls off lift in Stuart
cards.teaser: A 24-year-old technician was killed Tuesday morning when a customer's vehicle fell off a lift at Atlantic Tire at 705 Southeast Monterey Road in Stuart.
cards.body: A 24-year-old technician at Atlantic Tire, 705 Southeast Monterey Road in Stuart, was killed Tuesday morning when a customer's vehicle fell off a lift. Martin County Fire Rescue's extrication team arrived just after 6:30 a.m. and found the technician pinned between the vehicle and the wall inside the mechanic bay. He was pronounced dead at the scene. Stuart police say OSHA is involved and the incident is being investigated as a workplace incident.

cards.headline: Tampa Electric to cut customer rates 11% starting August 1, ending storm surcharge early
cards.teaser: Tampa Electric announced Tuesday it will remove a storm recovery surcharge from customer bills effective August 1, a month earlier than originally planned.
cards.body:
Tampa Electric customers will see an 11% to 12% reduction in monthly electric costs starting August 1, when the utility removes a storm recovery surcharge from bills a month earlier than originally planned. The change will lower bills by roughly $20 per 1,000 kilowatt-hours of electricity used. The surcharge was approved by the Florida Public Service Commission in March 2025 to allow Tampa Electric to recover more than $400 million in restoration costs following Florida's 2024 hurricane season. Originally expected to remain through August with removal beginning in September, the utility now says those costs will be fully recovered sooner than anticipated.

The surcharge stemmed from Hurricanes Helene and Milton, which brought extensive flooding and widespread damage from downed trees to West Central Florida. Tampa Electric deployed approximately 9,500 out-of-state utility workers during recovery efforts. Customers enrolled in the Budget Billing program may not see the full reduction immediately, as the program is designed to smooth monthly bill fluctuations over time. Tampa Electric said those customers will experience more gradual adjustments as the surcharge rolls off. The utility encouraged customers experiencing financial hardship to contact them about payment arrangements and assistance programs. The rate reduction affects approximately 870,000 customers across West Central Florida.

cards.headline: Martin County's Treasure Coast Square Mall redevelopment study sparks mixed reactions from shoppers and business owners
cards.body:
Treasure Coast Square Mall has remained a community landmark for many years, but recent discussions about its future have reignited concerns among both shoppers and business owners. In 2023, Martin County initiated a study examining potential redevelopment options that would transform the property. The proposed concepts include residential apartments, an amphitheater, and green spaces designed as an outdoor shopping environment. County officials characterized the study as a preliminary planning exercise rather than a committed development plan.

Business owners operating inside the mall are closely monitoring the redevelopment discussions and considering what changes might mean for their operations. Jessica Henry, owner of Plantitude and Flame, expressed hope that any future redesign would incorporate open concept stores while allowing existing businesses to continue operating. Ron Gustafson, who runs MVP Sport Cards, reports that his store has thrived in its current location and notes the business model has been successful. However, Gustafson has experienced persistent water damage problems and believes the mall requires significant improvements. He stated that the property shows signs of neglect but could recover with proper management and investment.

Customer opinions about the mall vary, though most express openness to improvements. Shopper Liz Permar called it a fun destination, while another customer, Kimberly Grucza, described it as an acceptable if not ideal location. Both shoppers welcomed the idea of updates and renovations. Permar supported the concept of a facelift, and Grucza indicated she would appreciate modernization efforts. Not everyone supports all aspects of the proposed redevelopment plan, however. Grucza voiced concerns specifically about the apartment component, noting that the surrounding area already contains numerous residential developments and does not need additional housing options.

County and mall leadership have maintained cautious stances on the proposal's future. Martin County Administrator Don Donaldson reiterated that the 2023 study was created as a planning exercise and remains in that capacity. Treasure Coast Square management similarly stated that whether any plans will be implemented remains uncertain. The redevelopment options outlined in the county study continue to be discussed among stakeholders, while shoppers and business owners await clarification about what changes the mall may experience in the coming years.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Mayor Sara Baxter drops commission race to run for Congress in District 22
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County Mayor and District 6 Commissioner Sara Baxter has dropped out of the race to reclaim her commission seat, setting her sights on a bid for the newly redrawn District 22 congressional seat.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County Mayor and District 6 Commissioner Sara Baxter has dropped her reelection campaign to run for the newly redrawn District 22 congressional seat. The district was reshaped after Gov. Ron DeSantis signed legislation in early May that shuffled congressional borders to give Republicans a larger advantage. "With this new district and living in it, it was kind of one of those lifetime opportunities," Baxter said. "The ultimate factor. I want to be able to help residents and help more of them."

Baxter is one of seven Republicans running for the seat and faces significant obstacles. Political analyst Brian Crowley notes that candidates must introduce themselves to voters across parts of Palm Beach, Broward, Collier and Hendry counties. Baxter was elected to her commission seat in 2022 without prior political experience and received a Trump endorsement for her terminated reelection campaign. Crowley says without a new Trump endorsement for the District 22 race, her path forward becomes steeper. Baxter must raise more than $10,000 to qualify by June 12, and funds from her commissioner campaign will not transfer to her congressional bid. With Baxter leaving the District 6 commission race, that seat is now open with no clear frontrunner.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County faces nearly $400 million budget cuts as property tax reductions loom
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County officials are preparing for what could be the largest budget cuts in county history, with funding for 30 departments potentially dropping from $609 million to approximately $210 million over the next two years.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County officials are bracing for what could be the largest budget cuts in the county's history, as proposed property tax reductions threaten to eliminate nearly $400 million from county operations over the next two years. County Administrator Joe Abruzzo announced during a budget meeting that if the property tax reduction passes, the county's budget for 30 departments could drop from $609 million to approximately $210 million, a loss of more than 65% of current funding. The Palm Beach County Fire Department alone stands to lose just under $200 million in funding under the proposed tax structure. The cuts would affect virtually every county service, including parks, libraries and roads. A major concern centers on the proposed $250,000 homestead exemption, which may not represent the final figure. Abruzzo warned commissioners that the exemption could potentially increase to $500,000, further deepening the budget shortfall.

County leaders are examining millage rates and identifying cost-saving opportunities, with particular attention on the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office budget, which has increased more than 216% over the past 20 years. To help offset the budget shortfall, county officials discussed various revenue-generating options, including charging for parking at county beaches. Commissioners agreed they do not want residents to pay too much to park but reached agreement on implementing beach parking fees as one measure to help bridge the funding gap. Mike Caruso, the Clerk of the Circuit Court and Comptroller for Palm Beach County, suggested increasing the limit on how much the county is allowed to invest in Israel bonds from 15% to 20%, which would earn the county an additional $3 million a year in interest income. Commissioners agreed the maximum millage rate will be set at 4.5 in July, with final budget approval scheduled for September.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Town Council approves new rules for President Trump's Mar-a-Lago helipad
cards.teaser: Council members in Palm Beach met Tuesday to approve new rules for governing the use of a helipad at President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago club, including strict usage limits and penalties for violations.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach Town Council unanimously approved by a 5-0 vote a revised fifth amendment Tuesday to establish rules governing helipad use at President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago club. The helipad, approved in October, will measure 60 feet in diameter and sit on the west lawn, the same location as during Trump's first term. In April, the Secret Service requested the helipad remain in place even after Trump leaves office. The town already approved construction of the new helipad to be built this summer while the club is closed for the season.

The amendment specifies that during Trump's second term, the helipad shall be used exclusively for transporting Trump for business related to the presidency. After his term ends, it shall be used exclusively by government aircraft for emergency use by Trump or Melania Trump, as determined by the Secret Service, with Secret Service personnel onboard. The amendment also permits emergency use by federal, state or local law enforcement, fire-rescue, emergency medical services, or other first responder agencies. All other use is strictly prohibited, including by Mar-a-Lago members, guests, private parties, or other Trump family members who are not protectees. Violations result in a $15,000 fine payable within 10 days, with each subsequent violation increasing the fine by $10,000.

cards.headline: Boca Raton Mayor says city will take varied approach to address property tax revenue shortfall
cards.teaser: City leaders in Boca Raton were briefed on Tuesday on the potential impact of property tax reform in Florida, with revenues projected to drop $8.14 million in the first year and $16.7 million in the second year.
cards.body:
City leaders in Boca Raton were briefed Tuesday on the potential impact of property tax reform in Florida. Deputy City Manager James Zervis presented to the council during a workshop, outlining how two random homes in the city would likely see a reduction of property taxes of around $2,000 a year. However, revenues for the city would drop $8.14 million in the first year and $16.7 million in the second year. The referendum before voters this November would raise the homestead exemption in 2027 to $150,000 and $250,000 in 2028.

"Assuming that happens, we'll definitely need policy direction on how we bring these different ideas together and deal with the lost revenue issue," Zervis told the council. The policy direction involves exploring other sources of revenue, such as higher fees and other taxes, cuts in services and raising the millage rate on property taxes. Mayor Andy Thompson said the projected shortfall in a budget of around $250 million is significant, but it can be manageable in Boca Raton. "My view, at least at the outset, is we're going to take kind of a hodgepodge approach," Thompson said. "We're not going to do all through one mechanism; there's a bunch of mechanisms to use to apply that, but my sense is we will want to test them all out."

cards.headline: Boca Raton adds trespassing signs at parks, trains rangers to address homelessness concerns
cards.teaser: Boca Raton's mayor is taking steps to address a growing homelessness problem in city parks, as families raise safety concerns about the issue at locations including Wildflower Park near the Intracoastal Waterway.
cards.body:
New "No Trespassing" signs are appearing at parks across Boca Raton, including Wildflower Park near the Intracoastal Waterway, as the city addresses growing homelessness concerns. Elina Gundersen, a parent who regularly visits the park with her four children, said the presence of homeless individuals has created discomfort. "It doesn't feel very comfortable having some of that homeless population in the areas where children would typically be hanging out," Gundersen said. She noted that homeless individuals spend considerable time by picnic tables and are taking over bathrooms. Mayor Andy Thomson acknowledged the issue is a concern for city leaders, particularly in Sanborn Square, Wildflower Park and Silver Palm Park. In February, the city passed an ordinance to add trespassing signage at parks to make clear they are not places for people to establish temporary homes. Thomson said park rangers are being trained to work more closely with police, functioning as a subdivision of the police department with greater ability to engage with homeless individuals.

Local nonprofit Boca Helping Hands, operating since 1998, is also addressing the gap in services. The organization feeds 160 people six times a week and connects individuals with housing and job opportunities. CEO Andrew Hagen said the organization is committed to helping people in need and getting them back on their feet. Mayor Thomson said the city is working on increased patrolling in city parks.

cards.headline: England's World Cup team trains at Gardens District Park in Palm Beach Gardens
cards.teaser: England's national soccer team is training in Palm Beach Gardens after securing a 1-0 win over New Zealand in a pre-World Cup friendly in Tampa over the weekend.
cards.body:
Manager Thomas Tuchel spoke about the team's preparation at the facility, stating "We expect to push tomorrow physical and from intensity and style of play, ball speed and everything, want to take the next step." Tuchel also praised the quality of the facilities in Palm Beach Gardens. Star defender Marc Guehi echoed those comments, saying "Great, fantastic. Everyone is super friendly and welcoming to us, felt at home straight away here, and in West Palm Beach. The quality of the pitch, really good so far." Guehi addressed the challenge of adjusting to Florida's summer heat, noting "First day was extremely hot. We've been doing better getting used to the weather, getting used to the conditions, definitely a big step for us."

At Gardens District Park, the fields were watered moments before the team practiced. Palm Beach Gardens Director of Agronomy Andrew Keller explained the strategy: "They get a little bit of moisture on the leaf blade and it helps the ball skip across the field rather than the ball catching on the grass and rolling. It helps them play faster so they can replicate what happens in the stadium. Each stadium waters before a game." England plans to leave South Florida for its Kansas City base camp this weekend, with the team's first World Cup match next Wednesday against Croatia. Portugal's national team is also scheduled to train on the same fields after England's departure.

An intoxicated man was arrested after threatening employees at a kava bar in Port St. Lucie, according to police reports. The incident occurred at the kava establishment in the city.

Police responded to the scene after receiving reports of the threatening behavior. The suspect was taken into custody and charged in connection with the incident.

hero.headline: PEBB Enterprises and Banyan Development complete sale of Lowe's building at Shoppes at Southern Grove in Port St. Lucie
hero.body:
PEBB Enterprises and Banyan Development have completed the sale of the Lowe's building at Shoppes at Southern Grove in Port St. Lucie's Tradition community. The transaction marks a significant commercial real estate deal in the growing Tradition area of Port St. Lucie.

The Shoppes at Southern Grove is located in Tradition, a master-planned community in Port St. Lucie. PEBB Enterprises and Banyan Development partnered on the sale of the Lowe's anchor building at the shopping center.

The sale represents continued commercial development activity in Port St. Lucie's Tradition community. The Tradition area has seen ongoing residential and commercial growth in recent years, attracting major retailers and developers to the region.

The transaction involves one of the anchor retail spaces at Shoppes at Southern Grove. PEBB Enterprises and Banyan Development coordinated the completion of the sale, though specific financial terms and the buyer's identity were not disclosed in available reports.

cards.headline: Mom Mobile brings prenatal care to Okeechobee County, where no hospital delivers babies
cards.teaser: Okeechobee County does not have a hospital that delivers babies, forcing many women to travel out of town for care. The Mom Mobile program is now bringing maternity services directly to expecting mothers in the community.
cards.body:
The Mom Mobile program, which originated with the Martin County Healthy Start Coalition, has expanded to Okeechobee County to address a critical gap in maternal health services. Andrea Medellin with the Okeechobee Healthy Start Coalition brought the initiative to her community after witnessing its success elsewhere. The 38-foot mobile clinic is stationed at the public library on West 16th Street every Tuesday, providing prenatal care and support in a safe and welcoming environment. The need was immediate, with 15 women served during the first three days of operation and appointment requests continuing to arrive.

Okeechobee County has no hospitals that deliver babies, forcing expectant mothers to travel to Fort Pierce or Highlands County depending on where they live. Twenty-year-old Evelyn Allen struggled to find affordable prenatal resources before discovering Mom Mobile. "I couldn't find any resources and the resources I did find you have to come out of pocket for it," Allen said. Medellin designed each visit to last approximately one hour, prioritizing quality care for high-risk and high-need mothers rather than serving larger numbers. Allen now calls the Mom Mobile "a blessing" for the support and resources it provides throughout her pregnancy.

Options under consideration include exploring other revenue sources such as higher fees and additional taxes, reducing services, and raising the millage rate on property taxes. Mayor Andy Thompson acknowledged that the projected shortfall in a budget of approximately $250 million is significant but said it can be manageable for Boca Raton. Thompson indicated the city plans to take a mixed approach rather than relying on a single mechanism, testing multiple solutions to address the revenue gap.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County bracing for largest department budget cuts in history due to potential property tax cuts
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County officials are bracing for what could be the largest budget cuts in the county's history, as proposed property tax reductions threaten to eliminate nearly $400 million from county operations over the next two years.
cards.body:
County Administrator Joe Abruzzo announced during a budget meeting that if the property tax reduction passes, the county's budget for 30 departments could drop from $609 million to approximately $210 million, a loss of more than 65% of current funding. The Palm Beach County Fire Department alone stands to lose just under $200 million in funding under the proposed tax structure. The cuts would affect virtually every county service, including parks, libraries, roads and other essential operations. Abruzzo warned commissioners that the proposed $250,000 homestead exemption may not represent the final figure and could potentially increase to $500,000, further deepening the budget shortfall. Commissioner Maria Sachs said the county would have limited options if the exemption becomes law and that if it passes, commercial properties and leases and rents will bear the burden of having to support government.

County leaders are examining millage rates and identifying cost-saving opportunities, with particular attention on the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office budget, which has increased more than 216% over the past 20 years. To help offset the budget shortfall, county officials discussed various revenue-generating options, including charging for parking at county beaches. Commissioners agreed they do not want residents to pay too much to park but reached agreement on implementing beach parking fees as one measure to help bridge the funding gap. The maximum millage rate will be set in July at 4.5, with final property value estimates also expected in July and the complete budget scheduled for approval in September.

hero.headline: England's World Cup team trains in Palm Beach Gardens after win over New Zealand
hero.teaser: England's national soccer team is practicing at Gardens District Park in Palm Beach Gardens ahead of the World Cup tournament. The team secured a 1-0 win over New Zealand in Tampa over the weekend.
hero.body:
England secured a 1-0 victory over New Zealand in a pre-World Cup friendly match held in Tampa over the weekend, with Harry Kane scoring the decisive goal with a header. Following this preparation match, the English national team has relocated to Palm Beach Gardens for additional training sessions before moving to their Kansas City base camp this weekend. The team also has another warm-up game scheduled in Orlando before the World Cup tournament begins. England's opening World Cup match is set for next Wednesday against Croatia.

Manager Thomas Tuchel emphasized the team's commitment to progressing during their time in Palm Beach Gardens. "We expect to push tomorrow physical and from intensity and style of play, ball speed and everything, want to take the next step," Tuchel said about the upcoming practice sessions. Tuchel highlighted the quality of the facilities available to the team during their stay in the area. Star defender Marc Guehi shared similar sentiments about the accommodations and venue, noting the positive experience the squad has had since arriving. "Great, fantastic. Everyone is super friendly and welcoming to us, felt at home straight away here, and in West Palm Beach. The quality of the pitch, really good so far," Guehi said. However, Guehi acknowledged that adapting to Florida's summer heat presented a challenge for the players. He explained that while the first day was extremely hot, the team has been gradually adjusting to the weather conditions.

The training facilities in Palm Beach Gardens employ specific techniques to optimize playing conditions. At Gardens District Park, staff water the fields moments before the team arrives for practice. Andrew Keller, Palm Beach Gardens Director of Agronomy, explained the reasoning behind this preparation. The moisture on the grass helps the ball move more quickly across the field rather than catching on the grass and rolling, allowing players to practice at speeds that replicate actual stadium conditions. Keller noted that professional stadiums also water their fields before matches.

England's presence in South Florida represents part of broader World Cup preparations happening in the region. After the English team departs for Kansas City, Portugal's national team will use the same facilities in Palm Beach Gardens for their own training sessions. This rotation of international teams demonstrates the area's importance as a training destination for World Cup participants preparing for the tournament.

cards.headline: Tire shop technician killed after vehicle falls off lift in Stuart
cards.teaser: A 24-year-old technician was killed Tuesday morning when a customer's vehicle fell off a lift at Atlantic Tire at 705 Southeast Monterey Road in Stuart.
cards.body: A 24-year-old technician at Atlantic Tire, 705 Southeast Monterey Road in Stuart, was killed Tuesday morning when a customer's vehicle fell off a lift. Martin County Fire Rescue's extrication team arrived just after 6:30 a.m. and found the technician pinned between the vehicle and the wall inside the mechanic bay. He was pronounced dead at the scene. Stuart police say OSHA is involved and the incident is being investigated as a workplace incident.

cards.headline: Wellington High School football team targets playoff return after four-year drought
cards.teaser: Wellington Wolverines football is working through summer training with a goal of ending a postseason drought that has stretched since 2022. Second-year head coach Pete Walker brings three state titles from his time at Glades Day.
cards.body:
Wellington High School's football team is working to end a postseason drought that has stretched since 2022. Senior Brady Seider emphasized the team's motivation to prove doubters wrong. "Everybody just looks at Wellington like we are a bunch of nobodies. We really wanna prove everybody wrong. We just wanna get there, see what it's like to win," Seider said. Second-year head coach Pete Walker brings experience to the program, having captured three state titles at Glades Day. Walker said he believes the current group has what it takes to succeed this season.

Walker credited his coaching staff and the players' commitment to the team's direction. "The kids bought in through hard work and team and those types of things. So that's the things that we're concentrating on again, and they're moving in the right direction," he said. Junior Danhoi Williams said the summer work focuses on building chemistry among new teammates and coaches before the fall season. "Just trying to get a winning season and try to go to the playoffs. You know, get them gelling, new teammates, new coaches. Just trying to see that everything is going right in the summer and head into the season with it," Williams said.

cards.headline: DAS Beer Garden in Jupiter plans World Cup street party with free beer for USA goals
cards.teaser: DAS Beer Garden in Jupiter is preparing for the FIFA World Cup with a promotion offering free beer for every Team USA goal and a street party planned for the final match.
cards.body:
Co-owner Alex Marquez said the World Cup brings an energy unlike any other sporting event. When the tournament starts, the vibe changes and everybody gets really into it because it represents your country, blood, and heritage. Marquez said the lower-scoring nature of soccer builds up expectation and when a goal happens, people really lose their minds.

Soccer fan Jason Pitman said he plans to attend the morning watch parties at DAS Beer Garden, including being one of the people eating donuts at 9 a.m. Pitman said he is optimistic about Team USA's chances, believing the team is talented and it is just a matter of putting that talent together. For the World Cup Final, DAS Beer Garden plans to shut down Town Center Drive and set up a big screen television across the street for an outdoor soccer street party. The tavern is located at 1203 Town Center Dr 116 in Jupiter.

cards.headline: Turtle Tuesday beach cleanup returns for 20th season in Palm Beach
cards.teaser: The community-led beach cleanup known as Turtle Tuesday begins its 20th season this week, with volunteers working to protect sea turtle nesting habitats during the critical June through October period.
cards.body:
What began in 2006 as a small team-building activity has grown into a two-decade movement uniting local residents, businesses, and ocean lovers in Palm Beach. Founder Gregg Beletsky said Turtle Tuesday volunteers have removed over 14,000 pounds of debris from Palm Beach beaches since its inception. The strangest thing found during a cleanup has been a toilet seat. Collected trash is cataloged with the help of Loggerhead Marinelife Center, and the town of Palm Beach picks up the debris after the cleanups.

The cleanups are strategically scheduled during sea turtle nesting season and run in partnership with both the Town of Palm Beach and Loggerhead Marinelife Center to protect fragile habitats when it matters most. The group meets on the second Tuesday of every month from June through October, from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m., at the north end of Palm Beach Island at Mediterranean Road and North Ocean Way. Gloves, trash bags, and other cleanup supplies are provided. Students can earn community service hours while participating.

cards.headline: Medicare fraud scheme tied to Delray Beach company targets same seniors again
cards.teaser: A Russian national linked to Sunshine Senior Solutions in Delray Beach allegedly continued billing Medicare through a Texas-based business after the original company lost its payments, according to court records.
cards.body:
Mike and Connie Parrett were among dozens of Medicare recipients who contacted WPTV after Sunshine Senior Solutions billed Medicare in Connie's name for equipment she said she never needed or received. More than a year later, a new Medicare statement arrived at the Parretts' home in Ohio, this time in Mike's name, from a company called Centurion Superior Medical based in Austin, Texas. Federal investigators link Centurion to the same people behind Sunshine Senior Solutions. A criminal complaint alleges Centurion billed Medicare in 2025 after the agency suspended payments to Sunshine Senior Solutions in late 2024.

Nika Machutadze, a Russian national, is listed as an owner in business filings for both companies. He was charged with conspiracy to commit money laundering in January 2026 and arrested in Texas the following month. He is currently in jail while the case works its way through federal court in West Palm Beach. Two of the six charges from Centurion on Mike Parrett's Medicare statement, all occurring during 2025, were denied. Dr. David Maimon, a cyberfraud expert, recommends potential victims freeze their credit and consider purchasing an identity protection plan, noting that criminals often share lists of identities with other fraudsters.

hero.headline: Cornell Art Museum in Delray Beach Opens 'Persistence of Matter' Upcycled Art Exhibition
hero.body:
The Cornell Art Museum at Old School Square in Delray Beach has launched Persistence of Matter, a summer exhibition celebrating artists who repurpose discarded materials into compelling artwork. The show aligns with the museum's commitment to blending artistic creativity with meaningful community engagement, according to Marusca Gatto, Cultural Arts Director for the Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority. Guest curators Mavis Benson and Pamela Lambie assembled a diverse group of artists working across multiple mediums, all using reclaimed objects as their primary materials.

The exhibition features works ranging from sculptures to installations to mixed media pieces. Among the highlighted artists is Autumn Kioti, whose creations draw inspiration from both natural and urban environments. Another featured artist, Mike Silverman, has created the Self-Reflection series using salvaged hard drive platters and printed circuit boards to construct reflective sculptures. Silverman explained that his work encourages viewers to examine their own relationship with technology and waste in fresh ways. "Every piece invites viewers to see themselves and their relationship to technology and waste in a new light," he said.

As sustainability becomes an increasingly urgent concern for communities, Persistence of Matter serves as an artistic exploration of how discarded materials maintain value and purpose. The exhibition demonstrates how everyday waste can be transformed into beautiful and thought-provoking art, fostering important conversations about environmental responsibility through innovative creative practice. The show remains on view through September 10, 2026, and includes a range of public programming designed to deepen visitor engagement.

The museum offers several ways to participate in the exhibition beyond simply viewing the artwork. Visitors can attend artist talks, participate in salon discussions, and watch film screenings throughout the run. The Cornell Art Museum maintains regular hours Wednesday through Sunday, opening at noon on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday until 5 p.m., 7 p.m., and 7 p.m. respectively. Saturday hours run from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., and Sunday from noon to 5 p.m. For more information about the exhibition or special programs, interested visitors can call 561-654-2220.

hero.headline: St. Petersburg Mayor Ken Welch defends hurricane response as challengers attack record at first debate
hero.teaser: Mayor Ken Welch faced criticism from nearly every direction during the St. Petersburg mayoral race's first major debate, with challengers attacking his handling of hurricane recovery, the collapsed Rays stadium deal, and transparency at City Hall.
hero.body:
Mayor Ken Welch faced sustained criticism from multiple challengers at the city's first mayoral debate, hosted by the NAACP St. Petersburg Branch 5130 at the President Barack Obama Main Library. The contentious event revealed the central issues dividing the crowded field, with Welch defending his first term against attacks over hurricane recovery, utility problems, transparency concerns, and failed development projects. Former Governor Charlie Crist, the early polling frontrunner, emerged as Welch's most aggressive critic, using the debate to argue that St. Petersburg has stalled under the mayor's leadership.

The sharpest exchanges centered on Welch's hurricane response and his decision to leave the emergency operations center during storm activity. Crist criticized the mayor for not staying at the operations center, saying "We need leaders who will be on the job." Welch pushed back firmly, noting that he only departed after his shift ended and the storm had shifted away from St. Petersburg. When Welch challenged Crist about his whereabouts during the hurricanes, Crist revealed that his fiancee lived in the hard-hit Shore Acres neighborhood and that the couple experienced flooding. "I'm disappointed in you, Mayor," Crist said. "You ought to be more candid with folks, and be more honest, and be more straightforward, and take care of places like Shore Acres and Southside." Welch countered that the city was thoroughly prepared, noting that 15,000 damaged properties would have been affected regardless of preparation efforts and that the city responded agilely to the disaster.

The candidates also clashed over the failed Moffitt Cancer Center proposal. Crist characterized the decision to reject the project as indefensible, arguing that the city lost the opportunity to bring a respected medical institution to downtown. Welch rebutted by explaining that the proposal involved not just Moffitt but also a partner seeking to build luxury housing, which required a $19 million city subsidy. He said the city refused to compromise its principles by providing the subsidy without securing additional affordable housing commitments. Crist broadened his critique to paint a pattern of failure under Welch, pointing to the collapsed Tampa Bay Rays stadium deal and problems at the Mahaffey Theater.

The debate also featured City Council Member Brandi Gabbard positioning herself as a substantive alternative to both frontrunners, Jail Administrator Maria Scruggs mounting a grassroots campaign, and former Shore Acres Neighborhood Association President Kevin Batdorf attempting to prove his viability despite lacking political credentials. Fire Chief Jim Large did not attend despite receiving an invitation.

cards.headline: Tampa Electric to cut customer rates 11% starting August 1, ending storm surcharge early
cards.teaser: Tampa Electric announced Tuesday it will remove a storm recovery surcharge from customer bills effective August 1, a month earlier than originally planned.
cards.body:
Tampa Electric customers will see an 11% to 12% reduction in monthly electric costs starting August 1, when the utility removes a storm recovery surcharge from bills a month earlier than originally planned. The change will lower bills by roughly $20 per 1,000 kilowatt-hours of electricity used. The surcharge was approved by the Florida Public Service Commission in March 2025 to allow Tampa Electric to recover more than $400 million in restoration costs following Florida's 2024 hurricane season. Originally expected to remain through August with removal beginning in September, the utility now says those costs will be fully recovered sooner than anticipated.

The surcharge stemmed from Hurricanes Helene and Milton, which brought extensive flooding and widespread damage from downed trees to West Central Florida. Tampa Electric deployed approximately 9,500 out-of-state utility workers during recovery efforts. Customers enrolled in the Budget Billing program may not see the full reduction immediately, as the program is designed to smooth monthly bill fluctuations over time. Tampa Electric said those customers will experience more gradual adjustments as the surcharge rolls off. The utility encouraged customers experiencing financial hardship to contact them about payment arrangements and assistance programs. The rate reduction affects approximately 870,000 customers across West Central Florida.

cards.headline: Florida Sen. Darryl Rouson accepts New College professorship, ends speculation about House run
cards.teaser: State Sen. Darryl Rouson has been appointed as a Presidential Scholar and Professor of Trial Litigation at New College of Florida, ending speculation about a possible return to the Florida House.
cards.body:
New College of Florida announced Tuesday that Darryl Rouson has been appointed as a Presidential Scholar and Professor of Trial Litigation. Rouson will teach courses in trial advocacy and leadership in public life. The announcement ends speculation about Rouson running for the Florida House. Facing term limits in his District 16 Senate seat, Rouson had considered seeking his former House seat, which Rep. Michele Rayner is vacating to pursue his Senate seat. Rouson confirmed to Florida Politics that he will not file for Rayner's seat. "I have heard the calls in recent months from many community members who have encouraged me to continue my service and seek election to the Florida House," Rouson said. "However, after much prayer, thought, and reflection, I have decided that I will not seek election to the Florida House of Representatives."

Rouson is a trial attorney and former prosecutor who earned his law degree from the University of Florida and was the first Black prosecutor in Pinellas County. He previously served as President of the St. Petersburg NAACP and has represented the Tampa Bay area in the Legislature since 2008. New College President Richard Corcoran called Rouson's distinguished career in the courtroom and the Legislature an extraordinary opportunity to learn from one of Florida's most respected legal and public leaders. Rouson's relationship with Corcoran goes back to Corcoran's days in the Florida House. In 2017, as then-Speaker of the House, Corcoran appointed Rouson to the state's Constitution Revision Commission.

cards.headline: Democratic House candidate Bryan Beckman accused of violating Florida election law in fundraising mailers
cards.teaser: Bryan Beckman, who qualified Monday as a Democrat for House District 58, sent fundraising solicitations that omit his party affiliation, violating Florida election law requiring name, party affiliation, and office sought in disclaimers.
cards.body:
Bryan Beckman, who qualified Monday as a Democrat for House District 58, sent fundraising solicitations by mail that omit his party affiliation from the disclaimer. Florida law requires disclaimers to include the candidate's name, party affiliation, and office sought. Beckman's mailers list only "Paid for by Bryan Beckman for State House 58" on the envelope, meeting two of three required elements. The solicitations targeted Republicans who have financially supported Republican candidates in this cycle and past ones, asking them to fund a Democrat trying to unseat Rep. Kim Berfield without disclosing Beckman's party affiliation.

Beckman signed the Statement of Candidate in both this cycle and his previous run, swearing he received, read, and understands Chapter 106, the statute he is now violating. In 2024, Berfield defeated Beckman by more than 13,000 votes, 57.6% to 42.4%, in a North Pinellas seat where Republicans outnumber Democrats by 8 points. That same year, Beckman's wife, Kathleen Beckman, lost her Clearwater Mayor bid. Willfully violating state law carries civil penalties under Section 106.265.

cards.headline: Business magnate Joe Strada launches Congressional campaign in Florida's 11th District with $5 million pledge
cards.teaser: Joe Strada, founder of the largest privately held family-owned air conditioning, electric, security and plumbing company in the country, announced a run for Florida's 11th Congressional District to succeed retiring Rep. Dan Webster.
cards.body:
Business magnate Joe Strada launched his campaign for Florida's 11th Congressional District after filing federal paperwork last week and formally announcing his run Tuesday. The Lake Mary Republican pledged to invest $5 million of his own money toward the race, immediately reshaping the competitive field where eight other Republicans have filed for the open seat, including former Lake County Property Appraiser Carey Baker and Lake County Commissioner Anthony Sabatini. Strada plans to run as a strong ally of President Donald Trump, stating that he will "stand with him in Congress to fight for our families and our economy." He contrasted his background with career politicians, saying the district "deserves someone who understands the challenges they face and the real-world experience to provide solutions we need."

Strada founded Strada Services, the largest privately held and family-owned air conditioning, electric, security and plumbing company in the country, which now employs more than 4,000 people across 13 states with offices in Clermont, Wildwood and Tavares. He began his career straight out of high school as a handyman at a bowling alley before establishing his own business. Working with his sons, Strada developed training programs that have graduated hundreds of tradespeople to address skilled-worker shortages. Strada, a father and grandfather, has been married to his wife Karen for 41 years.

cards.headline: Rep. Neal Dunn endorses former staffer Bea Valenti in Congressional District 14 Republican Primary
cards.teaser: Congressman Neal Dunn backed Republican Bea Valenti in the race for Florida's 14th Congressional District, crediting her with helping advance priorities related to agriculture, defense and military service members during her time on his staff.
cards.body:
Rep. Neal Dunn, who represents Florida's 2nd Congressional District, endorsed former staffer Bea Valenti in the race for Florida's 14th Congressional District. Dunn credited Valenti with helping advance his priorities related to agriculture, defense and military service members. He said she was instrumental in his efforts to advocate for providing back pay and reinstatement for service members who were unjustly separated for refusing the COVID-19 vaccine. Dunn called Valenti a fourth generation Hillsborough County native with passion for Tampa Bay and said he is confident she will be a strong advocate for the region in Washington.

Valenti is one of several Republicans running to unseat Democratic U.S. Rep. Kathy Castor in the newly configured CD 14, which is considerably more favorable to Republicans than the district that elected the incumbent two years ago. Under the new lines, almost 55% of voters supported Donald Trump for President while just 44% supported Democrat Kamala Harris. In addition to working under Dunn, Valenti served as a domestic policy advisor to U.S. Sen. Ashley Moody, worked in the public affairs department for the U.S. Navy and was a staffer in Trump's White House.

cards.headline: Deloitte volunteers support Florida nonprofits on annual Impact Day across Tampa, Orlando, Jacksonville and Miami
cards.teaser: Professionals from Deloitte offices across Florida volunteered with local charities and nonprofits on June 5 as part of Impact Day, an annual day of service that helps create positive impact for local communities and residents.
cards.body:
On June 5, Deloitte professionals from offices across Florida volunteered with local nonprofits as part of Impact Day, an annual day of service. Deloitte's Tampa and Orlando offices mobilized approximately 500 volunteers across 19 service projects. Working alongside organizations including Feeding Tampa Bay, Hillsborough County Pet Resource Center, Girls Inc. Sarasota, Ronald McDonald House, Habitat for Humanity of Tampa Bay Hillsborough, Goodwill Industries, Children's Cancer Center, 1Voice Foundation, Quantum Leap Farm and Disabled American Veterans, Deloitte professionals took part in warehouse sorting, food pantry support, landscaping, painting, camp assistance, pet enrichment and disaster kit assembly.

In Orlando, teams continued a multiyear relationship with Zebra Youth, painting a mural and improving the organization's space. Another Orlando effort mobilized 75 volunteers across three shifts to support The WASH Foundation, sorting and recycling soap and hygiene products to expand access to basic sanitation resources for vulnerable populations worldwide. In Jacksonville, approximately 100 Deloitte professionals volunteered at the Jacksonville Humane Society, the American Heart Association and St. Johns Riverkeeper, participating in river cleanups, animal care support and CPR and AED certification training. In Tallahassee, the Deloitte team sorted donations at The Salvation Army to support families facing immediate hardship. In Miami, Deloitte professionals spent Impact Day with The Posse Foundation, leading workshops on time management, wellness, active listening and goal setting.

hero.headline: Treasure Coast Square Mall redevelopment study divides shoppers and business owners in Martin County
hero.body:
Treasure Coast Square Mall, a longtime community shopping destination, is generating discussion about its future following a 2023 study commissioned by Martin County. The study examined redevelopment possibilities that would transform the mall into an outdoor concept featuring apartments, an amphitheater, and green space. County officials and mall management have both characterized the 2023 study as a planning exercise rather than a definitive proposal.

Community members expressed mixed feelings about potential changes to the mall. Shopper Liz Permar said the mall "has always been a fun place to go to" and believes a facelift would benefit the property. Kimberly Grucza acknowledged the mall is not her favorite destination but said she welcomes an update. However, Grucza expressed reservations about one specific element of the redevelopment concept. "I don't like the idea of apartments just because we already have so many," she said, citing concerns about oversaturation in the area.

Business owners operating inside the mall are closely monitoring the redevelopment conversation. Jessica Henry, who owns Plantitude and Flame, expressed hope that any future changes would preserve opportunities for existing retailers. "I hope if it goes through you know they do more open concept stores where we're still able to have our business," Henry said. Ron Gustafson, owner of MVP Sport Cards, reported that his store performs well at its current location. "The model of the mall store has worked for us. The store has been tremendously successful," Gustafson said. Despite the store's success, Gustafson identified maintenance issues as a concern. He has experienced water leaking into his store and believes the property requires attention. "I think it's in neglect. I think with some effort and the right management I think this could turn around," he said.

County Administrator Don Donaldson confirmed that the 2023 study remains preliminary and does not represent a commitment to redevelopment. Treasure Coast Square management released a similar statement confirming the study's exploratory nature. At present, no decisions have been made about whether the redevelopment plans will move forward. The future direction of the mall ultimately depends on further discussions among county officials, property management, business operators, and the community.

cards.headline: Stuart tire shop technician, 24, killed after vehicle falls off lift
cards.teaser: A 24-year-old technician died after a vehicle fell off a lift inside a Stuart tire shop service bay.
cards.body:
A technician was killed when a vehicle came off a lift at a Stuart auto shop. The fatal incident occurred inside a tire shop service bay in Stuart.

The victim was 24 years old. The vehicle crushed the technician to death when it fell from the lift during service work.

cards.headline: Mrs. Universe 2026 visits Stuart nonprofit supporting people with disabilities
cards.teaser: The current Mrs. Universe visited a Stuart nonprofit organization that provides support to people with disabilities.
cards.body:
Mrs. Universe 2026 made a stop at a Stuart nonprofit during her visit to the Treasure Coast. The organization serves people with disabilities in the Martin County community.

The visit brought attention to the nonprofit's work supporting individuals with disabilities. Details about the specific organization and programs were not provided in available reports.

cards.headline: Palm City resident Irwin 'Cy' Louis Seidel dies
cards.teaser: Irwin 'Cy' Louis Seidel of Palm City has died, according to Forest Hills Memorial Park & Palm City Chapel.
cards.body:
Irwin 'Cy' Louis Seidel, a Palm City resident, passed away in 2026. His obituary was published by Forest Hills Memorial Park & Palm City Chapel.

Services are being handled by Forest Hills Memorial Park & Palm City Chapel in Palm City.

cards.headline: England's World Cup team trains at Palm Beach Gardens facility after Tampa victory
cards.teaser: England's national soccer team trained in Palm Beach Gardens following a 1-0 win over New Zealand in Tampa ahead of the World Cup tournament.
cards.body:
England's World Cup team trained at Gardens District Park in Palm Beach Gardens after defeating New Zealand 1-0 in a pre-World Cup friendly in Tampa. Harry Kane scored the only goal with a header. Manager Thomas Tuchel emphasized the team's focus moving forward, saying "We expect to push tomorrow physical and from intensity and style of play, ball speed and everything, want to take the next step." The team has another warmup match scheduled in Orlando before the tournament begins.

Defender Marc Guehi praised both the facilities and accommodations in Palm Beach Gardens, stating "Great, fantastic. Everyone is super friendly and welcoming to us, felt at home straight away here, and in West Palm Beach. The quality of the pitch, really good so far." Guehi acknowledged the challenge of Florida's heat, noting "First day was extremely hot. We've been doing better getting used to the weather, getting used to the conditions, definitely a big step for us." Palm Beach Gardens Director of Agronomy Andrew Keller explained that fields were watered before practice to help the ball move faster across the grass. England leaves for its Kansas City base camp this weekend, with their first World Cup match against Croatia scheduled for next Wednesday. Portugal's national team is also scheduled to train at the same Palm Beach Gardens fields after England's departure.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Town Council approves new helipad rules for Mar-a-Lago
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach Town Council unanimously approved revised rules governing use of the helipad at President Trump's Mar-a-Lago club.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach Town Council unanimously approved new rules governing the helipad at Mar-a-Lago with a 5-0 vote on Tuesday. The helipad, approved in October, will measure 60 feet in diameter and sit on the west lawn, the same location used during Trump's first term in office. The Secret Service requested in April that the helipad remain in place even after Trump leaves office. The council's revised fifth amendment establishes specific guidelines for who can use the facility and outlines penalties for violations.

During Trump's second term, the helipad shall be used exclusively for transporting Trump for business related to the presidency only. After his second term ends, the helipad may be used exclusively by government aircraft for emergency use by Trump or Melania Trump as determined by the Secret Service, with Secret Service personnel onboard. Emergency use by federal, state or local law enforcement, fire rescue, emergency medical service, or other first responder agencies is permitted. All other use is strictly prohibited, including by Mar-a-Lago members or guests, private parties, other protectees, or Trump family members who are not protectees. Violations result in a $15,000 fine payable to the Town of Palm Beach within 10 days, with each subsequent violation increasing by $10,000. The helipad was built during Trump's first term but removed after he lost the 2020 election. Construction of the new helipad is approved for this summer while the club is closed for the season.

cards.headline: Boca Raton reviews impact of Florida property tax reform on city budget
cards.teaser: City officials in Boca Raton were briefed on the potential impact of Florida property tax reform, which could reduce city revenues by nearly $17 million annually within two years.
cards.body:
Deputy City Manager James Zervis presented findings to the Boca Raton City Council during a Tuesday workshop on the potential impact of Florida property tax reform. According to the presentation, city revenues would drop $8.14 million in the first year and $16.7 million in the second year if the referendum passes. The ballot measure before voters this November would raise the homestead exemption to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. Zervis outlined how two random homes in the city would likely see property tax reductions of around $2,000 per year.

Mayor Andy Thompson acknowledged the projected shortfall is significant within a budget of around $250 million but said it can be manageable in Boca Raton. Zervis told the council the city will need policy direction on dealing with the lost revenue issue. The city is exploring multiple revenue sources including higher fees and other taxes, cuts in services, and potentially raising the millage rate on property taxes. Thompson said his approach would be a "hodgepodge" strategy that tests multiple mechanisms rather than relying on one solution to address the shortfall.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce pastor charged with child neglect after five foster children found without food, working bathroom
hero.body:
A Fort Pierce pastor faces five counts of child neglect after authorities discovered five foster children in her home were denied access to food and basic bathroom facilities. Gwendolyn Rolle, 59, had been caring for the children, ages 4 to 9, after their father placed them in her custody. Fort Pierce police responded to her home on June 2 following reports of child abuse.

When officers arrived at the scene, Rolle's daughter opened the door and acknowledged that abuse was occurring in the home. According to the arrest affidavit, she had been reluctant to report the situation because Rolle was a well-known figure in the community. Police discovered that the children were being prevented from using the home's functioning bathroom. Instead, they were forced to use a bucket for their bathroom needs and were required to bathe outside on the front porch using a garden hose. The working bathroom remained locked and completely inaccessible to the foster children living in the home.

Investigators documented physical abuse among the children, including bruising on one child's chest. The children reported to police that Rolle frequently hit them in the face and head as a form of discipline. During the police investigation, Rolle arrived at the home and allegedly told one of the children that "you're going to get it" once the officers left. In addition to physical abuse, the children reported being deprived of food. They stated they regularly went without dinner and were often sent to bed hungry. Major Michael Santiago of the Fort Pierre Police Department noted that the children depended on meals provided by their neighbors to survive. "These are true signs of neglect," Santiago stated. "For any child to experience something like that is absolutely disgusting and tragic."

Two of the five children are non-verbal and attend a special needs school, yet Rolle was unable to provide the name of the school to authorities. This raised additional concerns about her ability to properly care for children with special needs. Following the investigation, the Department of Children and Families assumed custody of all five foster children and removed them from Rolle's home. Rolle was released on bond while facing the charges.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff's office launches campaign to stop scams
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office has started a new campaign aimed at preventing scams targeting local residents.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office announced a new initiative Tuesday to combat scams affecting county residents. The campaign aims to educate the public about common fraud schemes.

"We have to get in front of this," a department representative said about the effort to stop scams before residents lose money. The sheriff's office is working to raise awareness about various types of fraud targeting St. Lucie County communities.

cards.headline: Second suspect arrested in Fort Pierce homicide of elderly man
cards.teaser: A second person has been taken into custody in connection with the homicide of an elderly man in Fort Pierce.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce police and the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office announced a second arrest in the homicide case of an elderly man found in a tent. A woman has been charged with tampering in connection with the case.

The arrest comes after investigators continued their probe into the death. The first suspect was arrested earlier in the investigation. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is handling the case involving the tent homicide in Fort Pierce.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County and Fort Pierce set new anchoring limits to curb inlet congestion
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County and the city of Fort Pierce have established new anchoring restrictions designed to reduce congestion at the inlet.
cards.body:
Local officials in St. Lucie County and Fort Pierce have implemented new rules limiting where boats can anchor near the inlet. The regulations are intended to address congestion problems in the waterway.

The new anchoring limits apply to vessels using the Fort Pierce inlet area. County and city officials worked together to develop the restrictions aimed at improving traffic flow and safety on the water.

cards.headline: Three St. Lucie County restaurants get perfect inspection scores while three fail
cards.teaser: State health inspectors gave perfect scores to three St. Lucie County restaurants but failed three others during recent visits.
cards.body:
Three restaurants in St. Lucie County received perfect scores during recent health inspections by the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation. Three other county establishments failed their inspections.

The inspection results were released Tuesday. State inspectors check restaurants for food safety violations, sanitation problems, and proper food handling procedures. Restaurants that fail inspections must address violations and undergo follow-up inspections.

cards.headline: Yacht with seaplane hangar arrives in Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: A yacht equipped with a seaplane hangar sailed into Fort Pierce this week.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce welcomed an unusual vessel Tuesday when a yacht featuring a seaplane hangar docked in the city. The specialized yacht is designed to carry and launch a seaplane from an onboard hangar.

The arrival of the yacht highlights Fort Pierce's position as a destination for maritime traffic. The city's harbor facilities accommodate a variety of vessels passing through Florida's east coast waters.

cards.headline: Steven Brown of Fort Pierce
cards.teaser: Steven Brown of Fort Pierce passed away in 2026.
cards.body:
Yates Funeral Home and Cremation Services in Fort Pierce is handling arrangements for Steven Brown, a Fort Pierce resident who died in 2026. An obituary has been posted by the funeral home.

Funeral services for Brown are being coordinated by Yates Funeral Home and Cremation Services, which serves families in the Fort Pierce area. The funeral home is located in Fort Pierce.

hero.headline: Irene Veronica King of Vero Beach
hero.teaser: Irene Veronica King of Vero Beach passed away. Services are being handled by Fucillo & Warren Funeral Home in Manville.
hero.body: Funeral arrangements are being handled by Fucillo & Warren Funeral Home in Manville. The funeral home is coordinating services for the family.

cards.headline: Governor signs bills affecting Indian River County water districts
cards.teaser: Governor Ron DeSantis signed legislation affecting water districts in Indian River County, along with pension changes for West Palm Beach.
cards.body:
Governor Ron DeSantis signed bills into law Tuesday that will affect water districts in Indian River County. The legislation also includes changes to pension systems in West Palm Beach.

The bills were signed Tuesday in West Palm Beach. The measures address operations and governance of water management districts across the region. The legislation takes effect as specified in the individual bills.

cards.headline: Vero Beach woman killed in four-car crash on I-95 near Mims
cards.teaser: A 71-year-old Vero Beach woman died in a four-car crash on Interstate 95 near Mims on Tuesday.
cards.body:
A 71-year-old Vero Beach woman died in a four-car crash on Interstate 95 near Mims on Tuesday. The crash occurred on I-95 in Brevard County, north of Indian River County.

The woman was one of multiple people involved in the collision. Authorities have not released the name of the victim pending notification of next of kin.

The crash involved four vehicles on the interstate. Investigators are working to determine the cause of the collision.

The Florida Highway Patrol is handling the investigation. No additional information about the crash has been released.

cards.headline: Richard Winkler of Vero Beach
cards.teaser: Richard Winkler, a Vero Beach resident, passed away. His obituary was published Tuesday.
cards.body: Funeral arrangements for Winkler are being coordinated. The obituary was posted for family and friends to view.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast Square Mall redevelopment study sparks mixed reactions
cards.teaser: A 2023 study commissioned by Martin County explored redevelopment options for Treasure Coast Square Mall, including apartments and an amphitheater, leaving shoppers and business owners uncertain about the future.
cards.body:
Martin County commissioned a study in 2023 exploring redevelopment options for Treasure Coast Square Mall, including apartments, an amphitheater, and green space in an outdoor concept. The county says it was only a planning exercise. Shoppers expressed mixed feelings about potential changes. Liz Permar said the mall has always been a fun place to go and thinks a facelift is good. Kimberly Grucza said she likes the idea of an update but does not like the idea of apartments because the area already has so many.

Business owners inside the mall are paying close attention to the redevelopment conversation. Jessica Henry, owner of Plantitude and Flame, said she hopes if it goes through they do more open concept stores where businesses are still able to operate. Ron Gustafson, owner of MVP Sport Cards, said his store has been tremendously successful but has had issues with water leaking into his store and believes an overhaul is necessary. Martin County Administrator Don Donaldson said what started as a planning study remains just that, and whether changes will happen is up in the air.

cards.headline: England's World Cup team trains in Palm Beach Gardens after win
cards.teaser: England's national soccer team trained in Palm Beach Gardens after a 1-0 win over New Zealand in Tampa, using facilities at Gardens District Park.
cards.body:
England's World Cup team trained in Palm Beach Gardens at Gardens District Park after securing a 1-0 win over New Zealand in a pre-World Cup friendly in Tampa over the weekend. Harry Kane scored the only goal with a header. England has another tuneup scheduled in Orlando before the tournament begins. Manager Thomas Tuchel spoke about the team's preparation, saying "We expect to push tomorrow physical and from intensity and style of play, ball speed and everything, want to take the next step." Tuchel also praised the quality of the facilities. Star defender Marc Guehi echoed those comments, saying "Great, fantastic. Everyone is super friendly and welcoming to us, felt at home straight away here, and in West Palm Beach. The quality of the pitch, really good so far."

Guehi also addressed the challenge of adjusting to Florida's summer heat, saying "First day was extremely hot. We've been doing better getting used to the weather, getting used to the conditions, definitely a big step for us." At Gardens District Park, the fields were watered moments before the team came out for practice. Palm Beach Gardens Director of Agronomy Andrew Keller explained that the moisture on the grass helps the ball skip across the field rather than catching on the grass, allowing the team to play faster and replicate stadium conditions. England plans to leave South Florida for its Kansas City base camp this weekend. The team's first World Cup match is next Wednesday against Croatia. Portugal's national team is also scheduled to train on the same fields after England's departure.

cards.headline: Medicare fraud scheme targets Palm Beach County seniors again
cards.teaser: A Russian national linked to a Delray Beach company accused of Medicare fraud allegedly continued billing Medicare through a Texas-based business after the original company lost payments.
cards.body:
A Russian national linked to a Delray Beach durable medical equipment company accused of Medicare fraud allegedly continued billing the federal health program through a new Texas-based business after the original company lost its payments. Mike and Connie Parrett were among dozens of Medicare recipients who contacted WPTV after Sunshine Senior Solutions billed Medicare in Connie's name for equipment she said she never needed or received. More than a year later, a new Medicare statement arrived at the Parretts' home in Ohio in Mike's name from Centurion Superior Medical, based in Austin, Texas. Federal investigators link Centurion to the same people behind Sunshine Senior Solutions. A criminal complaint alleges Centurion billed Medicare in 2025 after the agency suspended payments to Sunshine Senior Solutions in late 2024. Business filings for both companies have listed Nika Machutadze as an owner.

Machutadze was charged with conspiracy to commit money laundering in January 2026 and arrested in Texas the following month. He is currently in jail while the case works its way through federal court in West Palm Beach. Dr. David Maimon, a cyberfraud expert who has investigated Sunshine Senior Solutions, said he is not surprised the same people are being targeted repeatedly. Maimon recommends potential victims freeze their credit and consider purchasing an identity protection plan, noting that criminals work with lists of identities that are often shared with other fraudsters.
